research_page.title: ALTITUDE-AD: Sabirnetug in Early Alzheimer's Disease (Phase 2)
research_page.description: A Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating sabirnetug (ACU193), a monoclonal antibody targeting amyloid-beta oligomers, in adults with early Alzheimer's disease.
research_page.takeaway_md: The ALTITUDE-AD trial evaluates whether sabirnetug—a monoclonal antibody designed to specifically target amyloid-beta oligomers—can slow cognitive decline. Results are not expected until late 2026, meaning clinical efficacy remains entirely unproven.
key_findings_md: No clinical results are currently available; the trial is fully enrolled and active as of mid-2026 ([NCT06335173](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06335173)).
research_page.methods_md: Phase 2, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial enrolling 542 adults (aged 50-90) with mild cognitive impairment or probable AD and evidence of amyloid accumulation. Participants receive intravenous sabirnetug (35 mg/kg or 50 mg/kg) or placebo every four weeks over an 80-week period ([NCT06335173](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06335173)).
research_page.trial_evidence_md: Sabirnetug's clinical evidence currently relies on the completed Phase 1 [INTERCEPT-AD (NCT04931459)](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04931459) trial, which demonstrated safety and central target engagement. Efficacy hinges on the outcome of the ongoing pivotal [ALTITUDE-AD](/trials/sabirnetug-nct06335173) study.
research_page.sentiment_md: Public perception is sharply divided: retail investors have generated significant speculative hype equating Phase 1 biomarker data with clinical success, while patients and caregivers remain largely unaware of the drug. Scientific media maintains a measured outlook focused on the drug's mechanism.
caveats_md: Investor and market enthusiasm currently outpaces the scientific reality, as Phase 1 data only established safety and target engagement, not clinical benefit.
relates_to_md: [Amyloid hypothesis](/research/amyloid-hypothesis) — Sabirnetug tests a specific refinement of the amyloid hypothesis by targeting soluble oligomers rather than fibrillar plaques.

trial_pages.title: ALTITUDE-AD
trial_pages.description: Phase 2 trial of intravenous sabirnetug in 542 adults with early Alzheimer's disease.
trial_pages.population: Adults aged 50-90 with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or probable AD and cerebral amyloid accumulation
trial_pages.primary_endpoint: Change from Baseline in Integrated Alzheimer's Disease Rating Scale (iADRS) Score at Week 80
trial_pages.why_md: This trial tests whether specifically targeting soluble amyloid-beta oligomers—believed by some to be the most neurotoxic form of [amyloid](/research/amyloid-hypothesis)—can slow cognitive and functional decline. It serves as the first test of clinical efficacy for sabirnetug.
status_log_md: **2025-10-27** — Registry updated to reflect active, not recruiting status, confirming 542 actual participants enrolled.

notes_for_editor: Phase 1 (INTERCEPT-AD) data such as 'mild-to-moderate ARIA-E in 5 of 48' could not be strictly verified against the provided Phase 2 registry text. It was carried forward as necessary context from the trials researcher, but marked unverified in the fact check.
